Every fishing license bears a number which is maintained for each renewal, and which must be located in a visible place aboard ship.
Vessels with a shrimping license may only be replaced in case of total loss by sinking, accident, fire, deterioration or by sale or conversion to another type of fishing, provided the actual number of ships is not increased according to the census of the National Fishing Commission. This must be confirmed to the Ministry of Commerce and Industries. The new vessels are not granted new shrimping licenses but are given the quota and the same license number of the vessel that was sunk, suffered an accident, caught fire, deteriorated, was sold abroad or was converted to another type of fishing or to another activity. The right to replace a shrimping vessel in the cases mentioned above is recognized for the owner thereof, who may sell it, convey it, or transfer it (Art. 7 of Decree 42 of January 24, 1965).
Any sale, conveyance or transfer or conversion of a shrimping vessel must be reported in writing on sealed paper to the Department of Fisheries and Related Industries.
Decree 77 of December 30, 1968 confirms the provisions of Decree 42 of 1965 in providing that the presentation of the existing navigation permit and the vessel's paid-up tax certificate are additional requisites for obtaining or renewing the license for shrimping or fishing for anchovies or herring. When a permanent navigation permit has been issued, it should be recorded in the Registry of Property.
The Department of Fisheries records the permanent navigation permits in a special book so that once registered their owners need not present them in subsequent years, except in case of sale, conveyance or transfer, or change of name of the the vessel. (Art. 1 of Decree 77 of 1968.)
The owner of any vessel engaged in fishing without possessing the respective license shall be punished the first time by a fine of B/1,000 for each ship, and the catch shall be confiscated and sold by the government at public auction. In case of a recurrence, the fine is increased to B/5,000, and the license of the ship's captain shall be permanently cancelled. In all cases mentioned above, the ship shall be detained until the owner pays the corresponding fine. A shipowner who does not request the renewal of the fishing license prior to its expiration shall be fined B/100 for each vessel with respect to which no application for license renewal has been made and the ship shall be detained until the license is renewed.
Owners of shrimping vessels that have been fishing in foreign waters for a period in excess of 9 months shall have the shrimping license automatically and permanently cancelled. The time period specified here is counted from the date on which the vessel stops fishing in Panamanian waters.
Another decree to be mentioned is 127 of July 28, 1964 concerning tuna fishing. It provides that in order to engage in tuna fishing in Panamanian jurisdictional waters the owners of foreign vessels must secure a license issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industries, or a license to fish issued by the Department of Fisheries and Related Industries, and a navigation permit issued by the Ministry of Finance and Treasury in such cases.
The tuna fishing permit is valid only during the tuna fishing season, commencing on September 1 and ending on August 30 of the following year, and it gives the right to fish for tuna in both of the coastal territories of Panama (200 miles), that is, in both the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans (Art. 3 of Decree 127 of 1964).
